M1_210210 is the fixed reference galaxy (LEGA-C DR2, \(z = 0.6542\)). In the
birth-cloud experiment the linked-bump fits rail the dust slope at the \(-1\)
prior edge with weak UV, while the slope-to-\(-3\) arm fits the UV bands far
better.

follow-up. Preparation started against `kriek_conroy_free_bump`; the Noll-law

Yes, both hit their prior edges. δ = -0.987 (16–84%: -0.997 to -0.967) is pressed against the -1 floor. E_bump = 5.86 (5.63 to 5.96) is pressed against 6, and 6 is just the top of the U(0, 6) prior, not a physical value. Both priors are set in `results/m1-210210-kcbump-2026-09-29/run3/manifest.json`.

You already asked for the fix on the same night, and it's the `wide` run (δ ~ U(-3, 0.4), E_bump ~ U(0, 12)). There δ settles inside the prior at -2.09. ln Z goes up by 32.6, photometric χ² drops from 89 to 47, and the u* pull goes from -4.3 to +0.6. But E_bump still isn't well pinned down: it's 7.9 with a 16–84% range of 5.1 to 10.4, and P(E_bump > 11) = 0.09, so the upper tail still reaches the new limit of 12.
